Overview

Built end-to-end, from wireframe to production code.

On Immersicom, the designer and developer are the same person. Every screen shown in this case study was structured, designed, and coded by Cesar Lopez — from user-experience decisions down to the front-end that ships to visitors.

  • Structure all user requirements for a correct user experience.
  • Create assets and creative materials for web, desktop, and mobile devices.
  • Translate designs and wireframes into high-quality, production-ready code.
  • Optimize components for maximum performance across a vast array of web-capable devices and browsers.
  • Build reusable components and front-end libraries for future use.
  • Design and write software technical specifications; write code and perform unit testing.
  • Work with business units to improve efficiency and remove barriers in applications.
  • Document processes for development projects.

The Problem

A showroom only works if someone can walk into it.

Trade shows and in-person demos are expensive, geographically limited, and easy to lose entirely — as many of Immersicom's clients did in 2020. They needed a way to put a product in front of a buyer that felt as convincing as standing next to it.

01

Reach was capped by geography

A physical booth or showroom can only be seen by whoever walks past it. Every prospect outside that room was a missed conversation.

02

Physical presence is expensive

Booths, hardware, shipping, staff, and venue costs stack up fast — and the investment resets every time the event ends.

03

Flat web pages undersell the product

A product page with static photos can't replicate the feeling of walking around a car, spinning a part, or standing inside a booth.

Process

From requirements to a shippable experience.

Each capability had to work as its own self-contained "room" while feeling like part of one continuous space — that constraint shaped every decision below.

01

Structure

Mapped every business capability — from gamification to virtual reality — into a navigable sequence of rooms with consistent wayfinding.

02

Design

Designed the showroom shell: curved displays, info overlays, and UI chrome that layer cleanly on top of real-time 3D renders.

03

Build

Coded the front end in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript — reusable components so new capability rooms could be added without rebuilding the shell.

04

Optimize

Tuned performance across browsers and devices, then documented the system so the team could extend it independently.

The Solution

One showroom, ten explorable capabilities.

Visitors move through a single continuous environment — each stop is a themed room built around a specific way Immersicom helps its clients sell.

Home

The entry point into the experience — a cinematic 3D corridor that sets the tone before a single click, with a curved central display and brand pillars built into the architecture: Visual Excellence, Creative & Technical Innovation, Superior Customer Service.

Real-World Proof

The same platform behind the Toyota Virtual Auto Show.

In 2021, Immersicom partnered with Czarnowski to build the Toyota Virtual Auto Show Experience on this front-end foundation — complete with "Let's Go Places" animated vehicles, environment changes, product specialist videos, two photo booths, and a Toyota theater with vehicle reveals, video, and a game.

Immersicom created the animations and the front-end and back-end programming; Czarnowski led creative direction.
